plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the complete DCGAN (Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network) architecture as two mirrored pipelines labeled Generator (left) and Discriminator (right), each spanning one half of the figure and delineated by underbrace annotations. The Generator begins with a 100×1 latent variable z, passes it through a “Project and reshape” step to produce a 4×4×1024 feature volume, and then applies a series of fractional (transposed) convolutions with arctan activations that progressively upsample through 8×8×512, 16×16×256, 32×32×128, and finally a 64×64×3 output image. The Discriminator receives either a real image x or a generated image x*, starting at 64×64×3, and uses strided convolutions to downsample through 32×32×128, 16×16×256, 8×8×512, 4×4×1024, before a 4×4 convolution collapses the spatial dimensions to a 1×1 scalar that is passed through a sigmoid activation to produce the probability Pr(real). All feature volumes are rendered as three-dimensional orange-shaded parallelogram blocks, with black arrows indicating data flow. This figure introduces the DCGAN architecture, which replaces fully connected hidden layers with purely convolutional operations to produce and evaluate photorealistic images.

discriminator input feature block labeled 32×32×128
discriminator feature block labeled 16×16×256
discriminator feature block labeled 8×8×512
discriminator feature block labeled 4×4×1024

bottom bracket/underline under final discriminator convolution labeled 4×4 convolution
small arrow from 4×4×1024 block toward scalar output
two tiny cyan square output markers representing the 1×1 scalar path

label below scalar output path: sigmoid
final probability label: Pr(real)
black outlines on all volumes and arrows

temporary glow around the active tensor block during animation

interactions.teaches: The two halves perform opposite spatial transformations: the generator expands a noise vector into an image, while the discriminator compresses an image into one probability.

interactions.teaches: The learner sees the exact order in which data moves through DCGAN layers and how each stage changes tensor size and channel count.

demo_steps.title: Generator expands noise into an image
demo_steps.narration: The trace begins at the 100×1 latent vector z, then passes through project-and-reshape and fractional convolutions. The spatial size grows 4→8→16→32→64 while channels shrink 1024→512→256→128→3.

demo_steps.title: Discriminator compresses an image into a decision
demo_steps.narration: The trace starts from an image x or generated image x*. Strided convolutions reduce the spatial grid 64→32→16→8→4, then a 4×4 convolution and sigmoid produce Pr(real).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique diagram matching the source: front faces are true screen-aligned rectangles with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z receding diagonally up/right. Overall world span about X = -8.2 to +8.8, Y = -1.0 to +4.6. Background white. Main block palette: orange front faces #d2825e, darker right/depth faces #7a3d23, lighter top faces #e6956e, black outlines #000000. Latent vector and tiny scalar markers cyan #9adfda. Generator header centered over X≈-4.0, discriminator header centered over X≈4.8, both with black curly overbraces. Latent vector z is at far left X≈-7.6, total visible height about 3.5 units, drawn as two thin cyan vertical rectangles each about 0.12×1.45 world units with a small dotted gap; label sits to its left, dimension 100×1 above. Tensor boxes use visual dimensions tied to the source labels: display channel count mainly as horizontal length, spatial size mainly as vertical height, and use a short constant receding depth for feature volumes. Equal tensor labels must reuse equal dimensions in generator and discriminator. Feature-block dimensions, as X×Y×Z world units: 4×4×1024 = 2.25×0.25×0.35; 8×8×512 = 1.25×0.45×0.35; 16×16×256 = 0.80×0.90×0.35; 32×32×128 = 0.45×1.75×0.35; 64×64×3 image = 1.25×3.05×0.06, rendered as a nearly flat vertical plane with an image texture. Generator positions, front-left-bottom corners: 4×4×1024 at X≈-6.9,Y=0,Z=0; 8×8×512 at X≈-4.45,Y=0,Z=0; 16×16×256 at X≈-3.05,Y=0,Z=0; 32×32×128 at X≈-1.95,Y=0,Z=0; 64×64×3 image at X≈-0.75,Y=0,Z=0. The generator blocks step upward visually because their heights increase, not because their baselines move; all sit on the same lower baseline. Discriminator starts to the right of the central arrow: 32×32×128 at X≈2.55,Y=0,Z=0; 16×16×256 at X≈3.65,Y=0,Z=0; 8×8×512 at X≈4.85,Y=0,Z=0; 4×4×1024 at X≈6.05,Y=0,Z=0. Tiny 1×1 scalar markers are small cyan squares about 0.10×0.10, placed at X≈7.8 and X≈8.25, Y≈0.45, aligned along the final arrow toward the Pr(real) label. The central arrow runs horizontally from the generator image right edge toward the discriminator start, centered around Y≈1.2, labeled x or x* below it. Bottom bracket labels sit just below the baseline: Project and reshape under the latent-to-4×4 transition; Fractional convolution under generator 8×8 through 32×32 stages; arctan under the final generator image; Strided convolution under discriminator 32×32 through 8×8 stages; 4×4 convolution under the final 4×4×1024-to-1×1 step. Generator animation sequence: z 100×1 → project/reshape → 4×4×1024 → fractional convolution → 8×8×512 → 16×16×256 → 32×32×128 → arctan → 64×64×3. Discriminator animation sequence: x or x* image → 32×32×128 → 16×16×256 → 8×8×512 → 4×4×1024 → 4×4 convolution → 1×1 → sigmoid → Pr(real). Sigmoid formula for the final label if shown in tooltip or annotation: σ(a)=1/(1+e^{-a}).
interactionPlan.notes: Implement each tensor as a BoxGeometry-like oblique prism group with separate front, top, and side materials so the source-style shaded parallelogram look is preserved. Use orthographic rendering with an oblique/sheared depth transform rather than perspective convergence. The final 64×64×3 image plane should use a low-resolution generated texture resembling the source: mostly gray/white blocks with faint blue patches and a yellow/orange patch near the lower right. The animation should not physically morph one block into another; instead, move a glowing dot or short arrow segment along the pipeline, pulse the active tensor outline, and briefly brighten the current dimension label. For generator mode, dim the discriminator half to about 35% opacity while leaving it visible; for discriminator mode, dim the generator internals but keep the central x or x* arrow visible. Keep text as crisp overlay sprites or HTML labels anchored to world positions, using serif math-style labels for tensor dimensions and larger sans-serif headers for Generator and Discriminator.

discrepancies: The discriminator side is faded by default, whereas the source shows both Generator and Discriminator at full contrast simultaneously.
The final 64×64×3 generated image appears as a mostly plain gray rectangle with weak pixel-photo texture and less of the slanted image-plane look seen in the source.
The discriminator transition arrow near the 8×8×512 to 4×4×1024 blocks is misplaced or points backward, making the flow less faithful.
Several tensor dimension labels are more crowded than in the source, especially around the generator middle blocks and discriminator output.
Some tensor block proportions are compressed compared with the source, and the final sigmoid/1×1 cyan markers are too small and subtle.
evaluation.notes: The architecture is recognizable and mostly complete, but default fading, a weak image texture, some proportion issues, and a misplaced discriminator arrow reduce fidelity.
action_items: Show both generator and discriminator at full opacity by default, or provide a mode that exactly matches the source figure before highlighting a selected pass.
Make the 64×64×3 output image look more like the source: a visibly pixelated slanted image plane with stronger texture and black outline.
Correct the discriminator flow arrow between the 8×8×512 and 4×4×1024 blocks so it clearly points left-to-right.
Adjust label positions and block sizes to reduce crowding and better match the source proportions.

feedback.rationale: All scores are strong and the remaining issues are minor generator-level visual fidelity and layout refinements rather than conceptual or plan problems.
